title: Try drawing with a local picture model, then turning the picture into editable layers
goal: Language models are poor at drawing by writing shapes; picture models are good at exactly what Ask gets wrong (a cat curled up asleep, a cat at a piano, a named style). Try generating the picture with a local picture model on this Mac and turning it into clean, editable vector layers, and keep it only if it beats today's way on the held-out test set.
notes:
The user, 2026-10-20: 'would it be a good idea to get reference images from the web to understand the intent better? Or use a better model, or something? what is the real fix to make it feel more seamless?'

Why this route: the current illustration work puts the craft in code (Sources/PhotonzCore/Illustrator.swift, IllustrationPieces.swift, IllustrationPasses.swift) and the single-thing route is a stored drawing set (DrawingLibrary.swift); both score well on cases they were built for and cannot draw what they were not built for, which is the one-cat problem. A picture model handles pose, scene and style for free, and tracing gives layers. Candidates to look at, not decided: FLUX or Stable Diffusion family through MLX or Apple's Core ML Stable Diffusion; for tracing, a library such as vtracer or potrace (check licences: potrace is GPL, which may rule it out). Waits on the held-out test set task.
acceptance: A local picture model runs on this Mac offline (the runner picks one that fits 64 GB beside the app, checks its licence allows use in a shipped app, and says why in the audit), drawing in flat vector-friendly styles from the request plus the style asked for

The picture becomes editable layers: colours reduced to a small palette, each region a named, filled path with curves, small specks dropped, a clean SVG export, under 300 paths for an icon-sized drawing. A tracing library may be used if its licence allows

Measured on the held-out set against today's Ask drawings: total, didWhatWasAsked, crafted, seconds per drawing, memory. It becomes the way Ask draws only if it wins on didWhatWasAsked without losing on clean and designed; otherwise the audit says by how much it lost and it stays off
An edit after the fact still works on the layers ('make the cat black', 'move the sun left'), since they are real layers

Audit under queue/audits/ with contact sheets of both ways for the same requests. Models downloaded for the try are removed again if it loses. Anything left rough is filed as a follow-up task if it clears the follow-up bar (queue/bin/follow-up-bar.md), and written into this task's log if it does not
